body:
By default `OPTION_OMP` is set to "on" in the tools/build_art script and in CMakeLists.txt.
If I invoke cmake with -DOPTION_OMP="off" the application successfully builds and launches after installation. However I haven't tested extensively and I'd expect its performance to be negatively impacted, at least.

If I leave the default configuration, with my homebrew based libomp installation, OpenMP is detected by CMake; however, for some reason, the compiler flag -D_OPENMP is not passed at compilation time, therefore the header omp.h is not included whenever because of the conditional check `#ifdef _OPENMP`.

It's not clear when this flag is set.

I think that it would be nice to have this working with homebrew and I feel that the fix should be fairly simple.

I'm investigating it.
